o.text: Borrowed from Russian болт (bolt), from English bolt.
From Proto-Common Turkic *čiš, ultimately onomatopoeic. Cognate to Karakhanid جِشْ (čiš, “an expression used by a woman when making a child urinate”).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *kïr-bāka, *kur-. Cognate with Turkish kurbağa, Kazakh құрбақа (qurbaqa), Tatar бака (baqa).
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *küs- (“to be angry, offended”). Cognate with Turkish küsmek.
Ultimately from Middle Chinese 疊子 (dep tsi^X, “small dish; plate”), via Middle Mongol. Cognate with Turkish tepsi, Karakhanid تَڤْسٖی (tewsi) and Old Uyghur 𐾀𐽶𐽼𐽻𐽶 (typsy /⁠tépse⁠/). Doublet of tepşi.
From Classical Persian حَدِّ بُلوغ (hadd-i bulūġ, literally “edge of the full age”), equivalent to hədd + büluğ.
Borrowed from Russian ваго́н (vagón), from French wagon, from English waggon, from Middle Dutch wagen.
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهِ ٱلصَّلَاةُ وَٱلسَّلَامُ (ʕalayhi ṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu).
